## Using the documentation

`docs/` is this repository's knowledge tree, governed by `docs/_system/constitution.md`. Consult it before planning, implementing, or answering from code, memory, or an issue tracker.

Route from the root. `docs/index.md` names the six kinds and the reader question each answers; every index below it describes its documents one sentence apiece, written so that sentence alone tells you whether to open the file. A kind index shows a subject subfolder as a count, not a description — descend into it rather than concluding its subject is undocumented. Open the documents whose descriptions bear on the task, never a whole directory. To search across kinds, grep the frontmatter `tags`, `type`, and `description` fields; the tree has no other search surface.

Documents own intent, rationale, and facts about the world outside this repository. For the repository's own current state, the code is authoritative — where a document disagrees with the code, the document is out of date, and reporting that is part of finishing the task.

Absence is not evidence. The tree holds only what some task required, so an undocumented subject is an unwritten document, not an unconstrained one.

`reference/glossary.md`, once it exists, is the project's domain vocabulary — one canonical term per entry, what the concept *is*, and the synonyms to avoid. Vocabulary bears on every task, so speak and write in its terms, challenge usage — the user's or your own — that conflicts with an entry, propose a precise term when the language in play is fuzzy, and when a task resolves a term or coins a domain concept, capture it in the glossary through the documentation workflow.

## Maintaining the documentation

When a task modifies the system, note its documentation impact and carry on. Before that change lands — before you commit it or raise a pull request — file a change note: when the first system-modifying task in the change completes, create `docs/_intake/change-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` from `docs/_system/templates/change-note.md`, append to it as later tasks finish, and commit it with the code. The note is a lead for the documentation coordinator, not a draft document — it records what the code cannot reveal, and the documentation itself is authored when the owner runs `OttoDoc intake`. Formatting-only, comment-only, generated-only, Git-only, and documentation-only changes need no note. The system has a boundary: `docs/`, Git's own files, and every path matching a `.gitignore`-syntax pattern in `docs/.ottodocignore` are outside it — a change confined to them owes no note, and a mixed change's note leaves them out. Run `OttoDoc assess` instead of filing a note when a particular change's documentation must be authored before it lands; a change assessed that way owes no note. Follow `docs/_system/constitution.md` for every documentation judgment. Use the project-scoped `doc_coordinator`, `doc_author`, and `doc_reviewer` agents when the canonical workflow requests those roles.
